nativeOutcome: One additional tenant household retaining the right to occupy its home because full-scope legal representation was provided instead of less intensive assistance
decision: Do not publish an Eviction Defense Collaborative dollars-per-10-QALYs price. The legal model itself is conditional on a judgmental five-point retained-possession effect, while randomized evidence conflicts across courts and comparison services. Research links eviction and housing insecurity to health harms, but it does not supply an EDC-specific causal legal-defense effect, preference-based utility change, duration, or person-level household allocation. Retaining possession is a legal and housing outcome—not a measured health-utility unit.

candidateEvidence.nearestEvidence: Systematic reviews of housing-stability interventions and eviction-related health outcomes, plus a Washington tenant-right-to-counsel mixed-methods study
candidateEvidence.studyPopulation: Heterogeneous US housing-insecurity populations, children exposed to eviction, and Washington tenants receiving legal aid
candidateEvidence.boundary: The 2022 systematic review found mixed and mostly low- or very-low-certainty health evidence for targeted housing-stability interventions, including legal assistance. The 2023 child-health review reports associations across heterogeneous eviction exposures and outcomes, not a preference-based utility decrement or the effect of counsel. The 2025 Washington study combines interviews with descriptive case outcomes and reports perceived stress and potential health pathways; it does not estimate causal QALYs. None can be multiplied by EDC's retained-possession scenario.

failedGates.label: Define and verify the retained-possession outcome
failedGates.why: San Francisco reports program-wide stayed-home outcomes across providers without an EDC-only cohort, common follow-up date, complete loss-to-follow-up accounting, or separation of continued tenancy, negotiated move, dismissal, time gained, shelter entry, and later displacement.

failedGates.label: Measure EDC's causal legal-defense effect
failedGates.why: The five-point effect is an MFI judgment. An older New York randomized experiment favored representation, a Massachusetts Housing Court experiment found no retained-possession advantage over limited assistance, and San Francisco's 18-point descriptive difference is neither randomized nor adjusted. A null effect remains plausible.

failedGates.label: Isolate legal defense from other supports
failedGates.why: EDC coordinates intake, limited-scope help, rental assistance, subsidies, shelter advocacy, referrals, and partner representation. Public reporting does not isolate which housing outcomes were caused by full-scope EDC counsel rather than cash, settlement-court processes, partner services, or underlying case strength.

failedGates.label: Measure preference-based health utility
failedGates.why: EDC and the legal-representation experiments did not collect EQ-5D, HUI, SF-6D, AQoL, mortality, or another person-level QALY input. Observed or self-reported health associations following eviction do not establish the utility gain from one EDC-caused retained-possession outcome.

failedGates.label: Establish housing and health duration
failedGates.why: Retaining possession at case resolution does not establish days housed, later eviction or homelessness, housing quality, the onset of any health change, or its persistence. EDC has not published linked 3-, 6-, 12-, and 24-month housing and health trajectories.

failedGates.label: Allocate benefits across household members
failedGates.why: The native unit is a tenant household, but QALYs are person-level. Public data do not report household composition, duplicate cases, which adults or children remain housed, who experiences a health change, caregiver and child spillovers, or overlap among household members.

failedGates.label: Identify EDC's incremental donor cost
failedGates.why: The $6,300 numerator is a historical city staffing ratio: a $315,000 fully loaded team divided by a 50-case deliverable. It is not an EDC invoice, current marginal case cost, completed-case denominator, or private-gift offer, and it excludes the distinction between assistance transfers and delivery cost.

failedGates.label: Reconcile public funding and benefit overlap
failedGates.why: EDC has not published eligible unfunded demand, public reimbursement and displacement rules, source-specific balances, attorney ramp time, or dated $100K, $1M, and $10M expansion plans. Housing, mental health, safety, school continuity, income, and public-cost pathways overlap and cannot be summed without a longitudinal person-level model.

illustrativeCounterfactual.arithmetic: $126,000 / [missing QALYs per additional EDC-caused retained-possession outcome] x 10 QALYs
illustrativeCounterfactual.publicationBoundary: No arithmetic result is shown because the model lacks both a stable EDC causal legal outcome and a defensible person-level health-utility bridge. The $126,000 native scenario remains visible as a conditional legal-outcome audit trail. Health associations and perceived stress relief are pathway evidence, not coefficients for EDC's rank or recommendation.

requiredEvidence: Pre-specify a duplicate-free EDC full-scope cohort and mutually exclusive legal and housing outcomes; link every eligible case to housing status at 3, 6, 12, and 24 months with complete follow-up and missing-data analysis.

Use randomized assignment when capacity is constrained, a credible vulnerability-score cutoff, phased rollout, or another defensible comparison to estimate EDC's own effect relative to the actual limited-scope alternative.

Collect preference-based utility and mortality for adult and child household members at baseline and repeated follow-up; model person-level housing and health trajectories, duration, spillovers, overlap, and instrument sensitivity.

Publish incremental EDC staffing and delivery costs separately from rental-assistance transfers, reconcile public and private sources, document eligible unfunded demand and constraints, and provide dated $100K, $1M, and $10M marginal plans.
